name: Stripboard sheet, 9 x 15 cm
summary: 90 x 150 x 1.6 mm stripboard (Veroboard style): 2.54 mm hole grid with copper strips running along the long axis.
description: A generic 90 × 150 mm stripboard sheet with copper tracks underneath. Hole and track placement is schematic; the solid export keeps the sheet envelope.
source: Checked by web search plus the Wikipedia stripboard article: stripboard is defined by a 0.1 inch (2.54 mm) grid of holes with wide copper strips running the length of one side, tracks are cut around holes to break a strip into nodes, the original Veroboard was punched through 1.6 mm copper-clad SRBP (FR-2) and some makers now use FR-4, and 1.6 mm is the thickness this entry uses. Retailer listings found in search sell stripboard in the same 9 x 15 cm (90 x 150 mm) sheets as perfboard, so the outline here is deliberately identical to the perfboard entry; I did not find a stripboard listing that gives a different size for this class. Not verified and therefore not claimed: which edge the strips run along on a given 9 x 15 cm sheet, strip width, and the hole count - 2.54 mm does not divide 90 or 150 evenly, so makers leave a margin. The preview shows holes and underside copper strips; the exported solid is a plain 90 x 150 x 1.6 mm sheet with the 90 mm side along X. The preview adds a schematic 2.54 mm contact layout, not a manufacturer-specific drill pattern. The export is the body envelope.
